Yes, that's the behavior I'd want. When I saved that example.com link, it didn't throw the whole thing away just because it couldn't pull the page's title and description. Instead it kept the link, filed it under **To read** like any other, used the site name as a stand-in title so it's not blank, and told me plainly that the page details couldn't be loaded and that I can fill them in myself through Edit. That last part is the reassuring bit — it points me at how to fix it rather than leaving me stuck.

And your underlying assumption is exactly right for me: I'd much rather keep a valid link I chose to save and tidy it up later than have the app refuse it just because the automatic bits didn't come through. The whole reason I hit save is that I want to keep the link — losing it would be the worst outcome. Getting it later from the source name and my own edits is easy.

So yes, this recovery behavior matches what I want. Good.
